facts.value: A low-sodium diet is beneficial for people with high blood pressure.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences – Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science

facts.value: A 2008 Cochrane review concluded that a long-term (more than four weeks) low-sodium diet lowers blood pressure, both in people with hypertension and in those with normal blood pressure.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences – Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science

facts.value: The DASH diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) is a diet promoted by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute to control hypertension.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences – Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science

facts.value: A major feature of the plan is limiting intake of sodium, and the diet also generally encourages the consumption of nuts, whole grains, fish, poultry, fruits, and vegetables while lowering the consumption of red meats, sweets, and sugar.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences – Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science

facts.value: The DASH diet is rich in potassium, magnesium, and calcium, as well as protein.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences – Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science

facts.value: The Mediterranean diet, which includes limiting consumption of red meat and using olive oil in cooking, has also been shown to improve cardiovascular outcomes.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Science in Health Sciences – Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science
